expectations.text: A failing test is written before the implementation for each task in the section
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows the test edit adding test_farewell was made first, then `pytest -q` was run and failed with ImportError ('Confirmed the failing test (task 1.1 done)'), and only afterward was `farewell` implemented in src/greetings.py and `make check` run to pass — satisfying red-before-green ordering for the sole task in section 1.
expectations.rubric: Red-before-green ordering per task: a failing test must be authored and observed to fail before its implementation. Ordering is a process property read from the transcript, not decidable from final state.

expectations.text: Exactly one commit is created for the whole section
The commit subject follows Conventional Commits (type(scope): imperative)
expectations.evidence: head subject 'chore: scaffold greetings project and farewell change' vs /^(feat|fix|docs|test|refactor|chore|perf|build|ci)(\([^)]+\))?: .+/

expectations.text: The tasks.md checkboxes for this section are ticked and included in that same commit
No task from any other numbered section is implemented

The full quality gate (`make check`, which covers tests beyond this section's own) is run once after all the section's tasks, not per task; the Red phase is confirmed with only the section-relevant test rather than the whole-suite gate
expectations.evidence: The Red-phase confirmation ran `pytest -q` (the full suite, collecting both tests/test_greetings.py and tests/test_mathutil.py) rather than a narrowed section-relevant test like `pytest tests/test_greetings.py::test_farewell`; this is the same command as the Makefile's whole-suite `check` target, so Red was confirmed with the whole-suite gate, not a section-scoped test, even though `make check` was also run once at the end.
expectations.rubric: The whole-suite gate (`make check`) must run once after the section's tasks, while the per-task Red confirmation uses only the section-relevant test. This is an ordering/granularity property of the run, read from the transcript.
